title: Micro-perturbation refinement of inner cavity spacers (layers 10-14) with ±0.5 nm step constraint
scientific_hypothesis: Fine-tuning phase accumulation in intermediate spacer layers (indices 10-14) of the 22-layer HfO2/SiO2 multi-cavity stack can flatten the 255-280 nm transmission profile without destabilizing outer reflector bands, yielding incremental target score improvement over the 0.5204 baseline.
design_principle: Preserve the verified 22-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology from prior iterations, but apply constrained micro-perturbation optimizer with ±0.5 nm step size specifically to layers 10-14 while keeping outer reflector layers (1-9, 15-22) fixed at their optimized values.
proposed_topology: 22 finite layers: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused silica
design_variables: Thicknesses of layers 10-14 (5 layers) with ±0.5 nm perturbation bounds around baseline values
Outer layers 1-9 and 15-22 fixed at baseline thicknesses
manufacturing_considerations: ±0.5 nm tolerance represents high-precision deposition capability
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional UV-compatible evaporatable dielectrics
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for layered media interference
Multi-cavity filter theory: inner spacers control passband shape while outer mirrors control stopband width
expected_advantages: Targeted optimization reduces search space dimensionality
Tests whether passband ripple is dominated by inner cavity phase errors
known_risks: ±0.5 nm constraint may be too restrictive to escape local optimum
Inner layer coupling may require larger perturbations to show effect
HfO2 absorption at 255 nm may limit maximum achievable transmission
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate for solar-blind UV bandpass filtering. Initialize all 22 layer thicknesses to the following values in nm from air to substrate: [57.29, 34.20, 36.06, 67.58, 24.38, 77.85, 92.06, 50.08, 24.74, 78.38, 49.64, 30.57, 22.93, 54.73, 63.11, 30.04, 38.67, 104.95, 82.26, 95.09, 38.40, 26.83]. Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with the following constraints: layers 1-9 and 15-22 are FIXED at initialization values; layers 10-14 (indices 10, 11, 12, 13, 14) are OPTIMIZABLE with perturbation bounds of ±0.5 nm from initialization. Evaluate transmittance at normal incidence across three wavelength bands: 255-280 nm (maximize), 300-700 nm (minimize), 700-1100 nm (minimize). Use composite target score weighting all three bands equally. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directive to isolate intermediate spacer layers 10-14 for constrained micro-perturbation testing. Differs from prior route_04 iterations by fixing outer layers and restricting inner layer search space to ±0.5 nm.
